brief.reader: People working toward their first $1,000 from Instagram
brief.problem: They post and hope, without a weekly record of what's happening
brief.outcome: They track views, link taps and sales weekly and share them
brief.mainPoint: Tracking helps you reach goals, most when written down or reported; here's what to track for $1,000
brief.slide2Check: Hook2 states the finding (tracking helps, paper helps more) as a promise of what to write: works without the 138 cover

slides.text: experiments agree: write your progress down

slides.top: Tracking a goal helped people reach it, and writing it down helped even more.

slides.text: Across 19,951 people, tracking worked best when it was physically recorded or reported to someone.
Each week, write down your views from Insights.
Then check sales against your target: $1,000 divided by your price.

chat.text: Weekly check-in: how did it go?
Here are my numbers for the week.

slides.text: Then share them. Reporting your progress made tracking work even better.
Comment PLAN and I'll send you the plan for your first $1,000, week by week.

caption: Comment PLAN and I'll send you the $1K Club page with the plan for your first $1,000. The finding behind this comes from a 2016 review of 138 experiments: people prompted to track their progress reached more of their goals, and the effect was strongest when they wrote it down or shared it. A notebook works. So does a note on your phone that you send to a friend every Sunday.
